full_target: For every prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer lambda with 0 <= lambda < p, and admissible lattice M in V(lambda), the L(K)-module M tensor_Z K is irreducible.
conclusion: M tensor_Z K is irreducible as an L(K)-module.

parameters.type: admissible lattice in V(lambda) over Z

hypotheses.origin: Exercise context: K is any field of positive characteristic p.

hypotheses.statement: K is a field of characteristic p.
lambda is an integer and 0 <= lambda < p.

M is an arbitrary admissible lattice in the characteristic-zero irreducible highest-weight module V(lambda): M is free abelian of rank lambda+1, its Z-basis is a C-basis of V(lambda), and U_Z M is contained in M.
hypotheses.origin: Exercise context, sections 27.1 and 27.4; arbitrary-lattice convention explicitly fixed in source-context.md.

calculations: Finite matrix multiplication and binomial coefficient identities; localization and tensor product calculations over Z and Z_(p); elementary finite-module calculations over the PID Z_(p).

primitives.meaning: The complex field used for the characteristic-zero module and the lattice M.

primitives.type: localization of Z at the prime ideal (p)
primitives.meaning: The subring of Q consisting of fractions a/b with p not dividing b.
The Z-subalgebra of the enveloping algebra generated by divided powers X_r=x^r/r! and Y_r=y^r/r! for r >= 0.
The scalar extension of the Z-span of x,y,h with [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=-2y, [x,y]=h, acting on M tensor_Z K.
